html:
The relationship between the United States and Ukraine faces significant strain as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expresses feeling "betrayed" by Donald Trump over military access to Starlink satellite internet services, raising doubts about long-term US support five years into Russia's war. This comes as UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham moves to "repair bridges" between the two allies during Zelenskyy's visit to London.

Ukraine Support: The curtailment of Starlink access, described by Ukraine as disrupting battlefield "missions" and its "military-grade" Starshield system, is attributed by Elon Musk to the US government. President Zelenskyy stated the Trump administration warned it could cut off intelligence and accused Donald Trump of "picking the other side," risking relations already strained by a US diesel deal with Moscow. Amid these tensions, Prime Minister Burnham affirmed the UK's unwavering support for Ukraine.

Mideast Tensions: Conflict is intensifying in the Middle East, with Iran-backed Houthis launching new attacks on the Saudi capital and striking the headquarters of Saudi oil company Aramco, prompting the US embassy to issue a security alert for citizens. Two cargo vessels have sunk in the Strait of Hormuz amid ongoing attacks from Iran, which has also threatened to target Persian Gulf digital infrastructure if hostilities with the US and Israel resume. Saudi Arabia has refused a request from Netanyahu to join the fight against the Houthis, while Trump stated the Houthis are "misbehaving very badly."

Global Economy: The price of diesel in the US hit an all-time high last month, leading President Trump to pursue a deal with Russia to release more diesel onto the market, a move described by Meloni as "risky" and alarming to Ukraine. High energy prices are contributing to inflation in the US ahead of upcoming midterm elections. Meanwhile, the International Monetary Fund forecasts a significant economic contraction for Iran, worsening its outlook compared to regional rivals.

Health & Humanitarian: Pope Leo XIV has been diagnosed with lung cancer and underwent surgery, with doctors reporting his recovery is progressing "normally" though it could take "longer than expected." Separately, Kenya has confirmed a second Ebola case, a relative of the first victim who had traveled from DR Congo. Aid groups warn of an imminent collapse of Sudan's health system amid ongoing conflict and climate change impacts.

Technology & Governance: In a notable move towards tech regulation, Australia is set to table legislation requiring big tech companies to allow users to switch off algorithms that recommend content, amidst warnings from its election commission about the "emerging" risk of AI in voting. Meanwhile, Donald Trump announced a new Super Intelligence task force with the White House AI czar Jay Clayton to ensure US leadership in artificial intelligence development.

Social Unrest: Thousands of student protesters in Albania have attacked government buildings in Tirana, setting fires amidst calls for improved university conditions and job prospects. In the UK, Reform UK faces a fresh crisis following reports of its councillors and candidates making racist and extreme comments, while a university club tennis team in the US was suspended over racist imagery sent to other schools.
